findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Record in Purpose (or step 6) why the custom `fast-export|filter|fast-import` strip is preferred over `git filter-repo` for the `.bridge_state*` path-strip + commit-map + tree-re-add work, or adopt filter-repo if no distinguishing requirement holds.
evidence: Plan: 'The primary reclaim is the proven length-aware `git fast-export --no-data | filter | git fast-import` history strip from A6-0c.'

git-scm git-fast-export docs (retrieved): --no-data / original-oid directives are for 'stripping blobs by id' — confirms the mechanism is legitimate git-native plumbing, so the concern is tool CHOICE not feasibility.

Retrieved prior-art (deployhq.com, gitscripts.com, studiok40.com): `git filter-repo` is the standard, recommended tool for removing files/paths from git history, including native path stripping and commit-map generation.
ABSENCE: neither Purpose nor step 6 records why the custom filter is preferred over `git filter-repo` for the path-strip + commit-map + re-add responsibilities the script reimplements.
findings.finding: The plan selects a bespoke `git fast-export --no-data | filter | git fast-import` history-strip pipeline (infra/scripts/reclaim_bridge_history.py) without recording any consideration of `git filter-repo`, the established purpose-built tool for removing a path from all history (which also generates a commit map and is the community-recommended successor to filter-branch/BFG). The plan justifies the mechanism vs repack (a genuine, correct distinction) but not vs the dominant path-stripping tool.
findings.location: Purpose ("proven length-aware `git fast-export --no-data | filter | git fast-import` history strip from A6-0c") and Preconditions step 6
scenarios: A reviewer or future maintainer must decide whether to trust/extend the bespoke stream filter vs a maintained upstream tool for the identical strip-a-path-from-history task.
findings.suggested_fix: Add a one-paragraph prior-art note citing git filter-repo as the established alternative and stating the specific requirement(s) (e.g., length-aware binary-safe data-block passthrough, deterministic scratch-ref output, in-tree assertions) that motivated the bespoke A6-0c filter instead.
